report_review.assignment_compliance: The report stays read-only, stays within the stated 1,300–1,700-word budget, uses five sources under the six-source cap, includes one metric comparison table and one bounded prospective protocol, and makes no Strata quality, acceptance-threshold, precision-change, performance, or implementation claim.
report_review.scope_depth_review: It separates tensor-boundary localization, recurrent-state trajectory, teacher-forced logits/NLL/distribution changes, and generated-task outcomes. It explains tail and scaling traps, distinguishes 16-bit store rounding from local FP32 accumulation, and describes where fixed-token and closed-loop comparisons answer different questions. The 16-prompt/128-token protocol is bounded and useful as a localization proposal, but has no sample-size rationale, prompt-selection rule, or acceptance criterion; it must not be treated as a qualification gate.
report_review.novelty_and_redundancy: The review follows the exact R788 next-scope recommendation. The diagnosis-and-metric question is distinct from R786's graph fan-in study and from R782/R783 type-boundary and kernel/API questions. R785's conditional mitigation scope is also separate. These checks used R788 review metadata, the index, and the target report; earlier knowledge-collection report bodies were not reopened.

source_attribution.assessment: The report links PyTorch numerical-accuracy documentation, a versioned Hugging Face perplexity guide, and three papers on low-bit transformer quantization, quantized state-space models, and teacher forcing. It states the evidence class and the limits for transfer to BF16, recurrent inference, and Intel SYCL/Strata.
source_attribution.correction: No cited page or paper was opened independently. The report gives an access date for mutable stable PyTorch documentation and a fixed version for the Hugging Face guide. Its source descriptions and numerical claims remain unverified by this review.

report_review.provenance_limit: The report presents sources as read-only evidence and proposes no code reuse. External observations do not establish Strata behavior, Intel B570/oneAPI/SYCL accumulation behavior, BF16 quality, performance, or 262144-token correctness. No license or source-file review was needed for the report as written.

next_research_scopes.title: Statistical evidence design for mixed-precision model-quality gates
next_research_scopes.finite_question: For paired autoregressive inference comparisons on a fixed evaluation set, compare how prompt-level sampling uncertainty, paired versus unpaired analysis, prompt/task/context stratification, multiple metrics, random seeds, and rare failure events should affect evidence strength and stopping decisions. Explain when token-level aggregation gives falsely narrow uncertainty and when prompt-level tails or task strata can change a conclusion. Do not define a Strata acceptance threshold or recommend a precision change.
next_research_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use primary statistical-method papers and original evaluation documentation. Compare a small number of coherent designs, their assumptions, failure cases, and the cost of coverage versus precision. Limit the topic to uncertainty, sampling, and evidence strength; do not re-explain the metrics or tensor-level localization already covered by R791, and do not survey numerical mitigations or kernel choices.
next_research_scopes.report_budget: 1,300–1,700 words; at most six substantive sources with exact URLs, one comparison table, and one bounded prospective sampling protocol.
next_research_scopes.prerequisites: Public methodological sources only; no local BF16 quality result or model/device measurement is needed to compare sampling and uncertainty methods.
prerequisite_evidence: The current index records native16_activation_pipeline.quality_acceptance as UNSET, performance_qualified=false, and physical_context_qualified=false.
Main reports the host lifetime fix is committed and a fresh v2 build is active, while no qualified native16 model result is available yet.

R791 addresses diagnostic metric interpretation and presents a 16-prompt localization protocol without statistical justification; this candidate asks how to quantify evidence and coverage, not which numerical metric localizes drift.
next_research_scopes.novelty_guard: Do not reopen tensor error metrics, teacher-forcing semantics, recurrent-state metrics, or precision mitigation. Compare sample units, paired uncertainty, stratification, multiplicity, and rare-event coverage only. Do not set tolerances, acceptance thresholds, or make a Strata quality claim.
